domain_applicability_diagnostic.full_local_argument: Take M=R^2 with Euclidean metric and curvature lower bound kappa=-1/16. Define f(x,y)=x+y^2 for x>=0 and +infinity otherwise. This is proper, lower semicontinuous and convex, with f*=0 and Omega*={(0,0)}. Start at p0=(1/4,1) in int dom f and take alpha=1. Then d0=sqrt(17)/4, a=1/4 and z=a*d0=sqrt(17)/16<1. Since exp(2z)>=1+2z, tanh(z)>=z/(1+z)>z/2, proving alpha<2*tanh(z)/z. Select s0=(1,2). For u>=0, f(u,v)-f(p0)-<s0,(u,v)-p0>=(v-1)^2>=0, so s0 is a valid global Subgradient. The update gives p1=(1/4,1)-(1/4)*(1,2)=(0,1/2). For k>=1 set yk=2^(-k), pk=(0,yk), sk=(0,2*yk). For every (u,v) in dom f, f(u,v)-f(pk)-<sk,(u,v)-pk>=u+(v-yk)^2>=0, so sk is valid under Eq.(2). Its squared norm is 4*yk^2 and f(pk)=yk^2>0. The update gives p(k+1)=(0,yk/2) and tk=yk/2>0. The sequence is well-defined and infinite, but every pk for k>=1 is a nonoptimal boundary point. Thus well-definedness does not establish interior invariance. This example does not contradict the potential inequality; the separate local repair supplies its proposed boundary-valid comparison.

operation_accounting.per_update: One selected Subgradient evaluation, one value evaluation, one tangent norm, scalar/tangent arithmetic and one exponential-map evaluation. A combined value/Subgradient Oracle may supply the first two in one call; separate interfaces require separate calls.

operation_accounting.terminal: A zero-Subgradient stopping test requires a Subgradient call at the terminal point, additional to calls at previously updated points. No terminal call occurs in the assumed infinite positive-step regime. Reaching f* with nonzero selected Subgradient yields a zero Polyak step and is excluded by that regime; no new stopping rule is added.

proofs.full_local_argument:
This is a local repair, not source text. Write a=sqrt(abs(kappa))>0.

1. Geometric upper support, valid at cut points. Fix q and x!=q, r=d(q,x)>0, and any unit-speed minimizing segment eta:[0,r] from q to x. Set e=eta'(r). For y near x write z=log_x(y)=b*e+z_perp in a normal neighborhood of x, and let P_s denote parallel transport from x backwards along eta. Define connecting curves F_y(s)=Exp_eta(s)((s/r)*b*eta'(s)+xi(s)*P_s(z_perp)), where xi(s)=sinh(a*s)/sinh(a*r). These curves start at q and end at y. Their velocities at y=x have norm one, so their lengths L(y) are smooth for y sufficiently close to x. Length bounds distance: L(y)>=d(q,y), with equality at x. For v=b*e+v_perp, first variation gives dL_x(v)=b. In the variation y(t)=Exp_x(t*v), endpoint acceleration is zero. Second variation of length gives Hess L_x(v,v)=integral_0^r (||D_s X_perp||^2-<R(X_perp,eta')eta',X_perp>) ds, where X_perp(s)=xi(s)*P_s(v_perp). Radial variation cancels from the length formula; the fixed initial endpoint and geodesically moving terminal endpoint contribute no acceleration term. The curvature lower bound implies Hess L_x(v,v)<=||v_perp||^2*integral_0^r(xi'^2+a^2*xi^2)ds=a*coth(a*r)*||v_perp||^2. Indeed xi''=a^2*xi, xi(0)=0, xi(r)=1 and integral(xi'^2+a^2*xi^2)=[xi*xi']_0^r. Thus H_x(y)=cosh(a*L(y)) is a smooth upper support for h(y)=cosh(a*d(q,y)), touching at x, with dH_x(v)=a*sinh(a*r)*b and Hess H_x(v,v)<=a^2*cosh(a*r)*b^2+a*sinh(a*r)*a*coth(a*r)*||v_perp||^2=a^2*h(x)*||v||^2. No exclusion of cut points is needed: nearby connecting curves need not minimize, and no inverse of Exp_q is used. At q, h is smooth in a normal ball, since cosh(a*sqrt(z)) is analytic in z=d(q,y)^2 near zero, and Hess h at q equals a^2*metric.

2. Distribution comparison. Let gamma be any unit-speed geodesic and u(t)=h(gamma(t)). The supports imply u''<=a^2*u in distributions, including cut points, as follows. On a compact interval where d(q,gamma(t)) is bounded away from zero, minimizing segments have bounded lengths and initial directions in a compact unit tangent sphere. Their base points remain in a compact ball by finite-dimensional completeness. The variation construction depends smoothly on these data. Its connecting velocities remain uniformly nonzero in sufficiently small endpoint neighborhoods, so its lengths and their first two derivatives are uniformly bounded there. Consequently the upper supports along gamma have a locally uniform upper bound B on their second derivatives. Taylor expansion at their contact points gives u(t+h)+u(t-h)-2u(t)<=B*h^2 for sufficiently small h, proving local semiconcavity. Near q the smooth formula applies. A semiconcave function has distribution second derivative a measure with nonpositive singular part. At almost every point it has a second-order expansion; comparison with its touching smooth upper support gives u''_ac(t)<=a^2*u(t). Hence mu=u''-a^2*u dt<=0. The right derivative at the initial time exists and is finite. Solving this scalar linear equation in measures gives, for t>=0, u(t)=u(0)*cosh(a*t)+u'_+(0)*sinh(a*t)/a+integral_(0,t) sinh(a*(t-s))/a dmu(s). The kernel is nonnegative, so u(t)<=u(0)*cosh(a*t)+u'_+(0)*sinh(a*t)/a. This holds on each compact interval, hence for every finite t, without requiring gamma to minimize.

3. Boundary Subgradient transfer. Take p,q in dom f, D=d(p,q)>0 and an existing nonzero s in partial f(p). Weak convexity supplies a minimizing domain-contained segment from p to q with initial unit vector w. Its [0,1] initial velocity is D*w. Eq.(2) gives <s,D*w><=f(q)-f(p)=-Delta, where Delta=f(p)-f(q). For v=-s/||s||, therefore <w,v>>=Delta/(D*||s||). Reverse that segment to construct the support of part 1 at p; its final radial unit vector is -w. Along gamma(t)=Exp_p(t*v), the touching upper support gives u'_+(0)<=-a*sinh(a*D)*<w,v><=-a*sinh(a*D)*Delta/(D*||s||). Part 2 yields, with E=d(gamma(t),q), cosh(a*E)<=cosh(a*D)*cosh(a*t)-sinh(a*D)*sinh(a*t)*Delta/(D*||s||). Only an existing global Subgradient at a domain point was used. Interior membership and domain membership of the new endpoint are unnecessary for this distance comparison.

4. Scalar passage. Phi(z)=cosh(a*sqrt(z)) is convex for z>=0: its second derivative has the sign of u*cosh(u)-sinh(u), whose derivative is u*sinh(u)>=0 and whose value at zero is zero. Its tangent bound at D^2 implies E^2-D^2<=2*D/(a*sinh(a*D))*(cosh(a*E)-cosh(a*D)). Also cosh(u)-1<=u*sinh(u)/2 for u>=0, because (cosh(u)-1)/sinh(u)=tanh(u/2)<=u/2, with the continuous value at zero. Substituting the comparison gives E^2<=D^2+H(t)*(a*D*coth(a*D)*t^2-2*t*Delta/||s||), where H(t)=sinh(a*t)/(a*t)>=1, continuously H(0)=1. In the application D and t are positive.

5. Original Lemma 4. Lower semicontinuity makes Omega* closed. Completeness in finite dimension makes closed bounded balls compact. A minimizing sequence for dist(p0,Omega*) has a convergent subsequence in Omega*, giving a nearest qbar and D0=d0. Fix any such qbar and any permitted sequence. Positive Polyak steps imply Delta_k=f(pk)-f*>0, so pk!=qbar and Dk>0. Well-definedness supplies the finite values and existing Subgradients needed at all computed points, without interior invariance. The function z*coth(z) increases for z>0: its derivative has numerator sinh(z)*cosh(z)-z, whose derivative is 2*sinh(z)^2>=0 and whose value at zero is zero. Assuming Dk<=d0, apply part 4 at pk with q=qbar, s=sk and tk=alpha*Delta_k/||sk||. Then D(k+1)^2<=Dk^2+H(tk)*alpha^2*Delta_k^2/||sk||^2*(a*d0*coth(a*d0)-2/alpha)=Dk^2-H(tk)*C*alpha^2*Delta_k^2/||sk||^2<=Dk^2-C*alpha^2*Delta_k^2/||sk||^2. The parameter interval gives C>0, hence D(k+1)<=Dk<=d0, closing induction from D0=d0. This proves the printed Lemma 4 for every permitted fixed alpha, sequence and nearest qbar, retaining alpha^2.

No Lipschitz bound, full-domain finiteness, reduced stepsize interval, interior invariance, unconditional Algorithm existence, terminal Oracle guarantee or unrestricted Oracle Complexity is added or concluded. The later printed Theorem 4 rate is outside this argument.

assumptions: Omega* is nonempty and p0 is in int dom f.
pk is generated by Algorithm 1 with Strategy 2: sk in partial f(pk), tk=alpha*(f(pk)-f*)/||sk|| and p(k+1)=Exp_pk(-tk*sk/||sk||).
The source assumes this sequence is well-defined and infinite, with positive steps and nonzero selected Subgradients.
statement.conclusion: d(p(k+1),qbar)^2 <= d(pk,qbar)^2-C*alpha^2*(f(pk)-f*)^2/||sk||^2 for every k>=0; in particular d(pk,qbar)<=d0.
statement.objects_and_definitions: M is a finite-dimensional complete Riemannian manifold with sectional curvature bounded below by kappa<0; d and tangent norms are Riemannian. f:M->R union {+infinity} is proper, convex and lower semicontinuous. Its domain is weakly convex: each pair of domain points admits a minimizing geodesic contained in dom f. Convexity holds along every domain-contained geodesic. For p in dom f, s belongs to partial f(p) iff f(q)>=f(p)+<s,eta'(0)> for every q in dom f and every domain-contained geodesic eta:[0,1] from p to q, as in Eq.(2). Omega*=argmin f, f*=inf f. Set a=sqrt(abs(kappa)), d0=dist(p0,Omega*)>0, choose qbar in Omega* with d(p0,qbar)=d0, and set C=2/alpha-a*d0/tanh(a*d0).
statement.parameter_domains: kappa<0, d0>0, 0<alpha<2*tanh(a*d0)/(a*d0), hence C>0. No global Lipschitz constant is required.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every fixed alpha in the stated interval, every sequence satisfying the standing assumptions, every fixed nearest minimizer qbar satisfying Eq.(12), and every k=0,1,... . No probabilistic assertion is made.
